nodes.title: ArticleNameClaim
nodes.description:
A contributor, publication inference, or import supplies a name in a specific language.

A name can be regional, not tied to someone's plot, so it records a region instead of a profile context: a place by ID or in the contributor's words ("macaxeira" in Pernambuco, or the whole Nordeste). Its provenance says who, without a context.

Open question: is the region optional, with no region meaning the name isn't regional?

nodes.title: ConsolidateArticleNames
nodes.description: Group equivalent names by language and place. Keep the original spelling, sources and locality. Leave gender unset when missing.

nodes.title: NamesByArticleId
nodes.description: Localized names with spelling, gender and sources. Open question: which source languages should we include?

nodes.title: BuildArticlePathIndex
nodes.description: Build one canonical localized path per article. Deduplicate aliases from names and identifiers such as GBIF, Wikidata and Syntropedia.

nodes.title: ArticlesByPath
nodes.description: Index canonical paths and aliases by URL. Each alias points to its canonical path.

nodes.title: GbifTaxonIdClaim
nodes.description:
A contributor proposes a GBIF taxon ID for a plant or animal.

For the 1st version of the claim, we'd always assume checklist key `7ddf754f-d193-4cc9-b351-99906754a03b`, instead of requiring users to send the GBIF checklist key.

nodes.title: WikidataRecordReceived
nodes.description:
The Wikidata entity for an article, fetched as Special:EntityData JSON. Keep the whole entity with its revision, the request and fetch time, and the selection it was fetched for (captured when the fetch started, so a late response keeps it).

This allows us to derive multiple types of properties as we discover valuable insights from Wikidata.

nodes.title: SelectGbifTaxonId
nodes.description:
Prefer an approved claim, then an unambiguous Wikidata ID, then a pending claim. Ignore rejected claims, and sources hidden in ClaimVisibilityById (such as a censored `WRONG_ENTITY` report). Resolve legacy Backbone IDs in the selected checklist before comparison or fetch.

Each taxon ID goes to the article whose source was accepted first: the claim's acceptance, or the Wikidata record's arrival. Other articles' sources for the same taxon ID go to GbifTaxonIdConflicts instead, and those articles get no taxon ID until the conflict is resolved (for example, by rejecting one of the claims, which hands the ID to the next earliest source).

Keeps the ID provenance for presentation purposes, such as warning when the GBIF data came from an ID whose claim is not yet verified/approved.

nodes.title: ArticlesByGbifTaxonId
nodes.description:
Index articles by the selected GBIF taxon ID and include the checklist key. One article per taxon ID: competing sources are in GbifTaxonIdConflicts. For provenance, keep Wikidata attribution or the contributor claim and its evaluation.

This is later used by transformations which match GBIF data to articles in a quick look-up.

It's also used to trigger GBIF data fetching.

nodes.title: GbifTaxonMetadataReceived
nodes.description: A taxon metadata response with the fetch time and the checklist and taxon selection used for the request.

nodes.title: ProjectGbifTaxonomy
nodes.description: Project taxonomy from the latest successful metadata fetch for the current selection.

nodes.title: GbifTaxonomyByArticleId
nodes.description: The selected taxon's group and ordered classification, with their source observation.

nodes.title: GbifOccurrenceSamplesByArticleId
nodes.description: A sample of detections with record and dataset IDs, date, basis, matched taxon and optional place match. Roll up counts by place and its ancestors. Counts describe the sample. Look up the fetch date in the observation.

nodes.title: HeightClaim
nodes.description:
A person, inference, or Syntropedia provides a height range. Bounds are optional and ordered when both exist.

A person's provenance names them and the profile context the claim comes from: one they pick when submitting, their latest by default. The claim stays anchored on that context when they start a new one. The claim itself adds when it held and how they grew the plant.

Open question: which practice questions are height's own, and which form a shared set (planting method, ground cover, pesticides) reused across plant properties? Some may belong on the context instead.

nodes.title: SummarizeArticleHeights
nodes.description:
Summarize observed bounds in centimeters. Keep cultivar observations and parent bounds alongside each other with their origins.

Keep each claim's profile context beside its bounds, so readers' pages can rank them by affinity using height's relevant dimensions. Claims without a context still count.

Open question: is a single overall range still useful once readers see ranges ranked by affinity?

nodes.title: HeightSummariesByArticleId
nodes.description: A situated height summary in centimeters, with a separate parent range for a cultivar.

nodes.title: AssembleArticleDocument
nodes.description: Combine resolved properties into a consistent article projection for downstream readers.

nodes.title: ArticleDocument
nodes.description: Page data combining names, paths, native range, occurrence sample, taxonomy, height and images. Use observation IDs to look up GBIF evidence.

pt.text: Nativa do sudeste da Austrália, incluindo a Tasmânia.

nodes.title: GeographicalOriginClaim
nodes.description: A contributor proposes a sourced description of the taxon's native range in a specific language.

exampleData.text: Nativa do sudeste da Austrália, incluindo a Tasmânia.

nodes.title: ResolveGeographicalOrigin
nodes.description: Resolve approved contributor text per language. Use the latest matching taxon metadata fetch and reference it when it contains explicit native rows.

nodes.title: GeographicalOriginByArticleId
nodes.description: Localized contributor text alongside a GBIF observation reference. For GBIF, display explicit native rows using equivalent PLACE names when available, with the original locality as fallback.

pt.text: Nativa do sudeste da Austrália, incluindo a Tasmânia.

nodes.title: GbifTaxonOccurrencesReceived
nodes.description: A bounded detection search for the selected taxon, with the filters, pagination, fetch time and selection used for the request. Images come from each occurrence's media, so one search feeds both places and galleries. Keep matched taxa to distinguish exact records, synonyms and descendants.

nodes.title: LinkGbifOccurrencesToPlaces
nodes.description: Use the latest matching search. Link each record to the smallest supported place containing its reliable extent, respecting uncertainty and withheld or generalized locations. Fall back to a reliable area ID or country. Keep unresolved records and record how matches were made. Create PLACE articles only for surfaced places.

nodes.title: ImportGbifOccurrenceImages
nodes.description: Use the media of the latest matching occurrences observation and the existing provider photo import. Keep the source occurrence URL, credits and license on the imported assets.

nodes.title: GbifImageAssetsByArticleId
nodes.description: Imported GBIF media assets with their source observation. Assets follow the shared moderation lifecycle.

nodes.title: IndexGbifObservation
nodes.description: Index each successful fetch by observation ID. Keep its result, request filters and the taxon selection as captured when the fetch started. A late response keeps its original selection.

nodes.title: GbifObservationsById
nodes.description: Shared GBIF observations by ID. Each holds the result, fetch time, checklist and taxon selection with its provenance. Derived properties reference these observations.

nodes.title: FetchGbifTaxonData
nodes.description:
Request GBIF metadata and occurrences for an article's taxon selection.

Fires when ArticlesByGbifTaxonId changes for an article (a new selection, a different taxon or checklist), and from a periodic sweep for refreshes. Like FetchWikidataEntity, it reads only the selection, and the workflow owns freshness, idempotency and retries.

Metadata and occurrences are separate executions, so one failing doesn't refetch the other. Both refresh every 2 weeks for now, configurable later. Occurrences gain little from refreshing sooner: the article shows a bounded sample, and each refresh can relink places and import or drop gallery images. Keep the occurrence query deterministic, so a refresh changes the sample only when GBIF's records change.

GBIF has no revision to compare, so every refresh records a full response. A taxon missing from the checklist records ExternalFetchFailed with `NOT_FOUND`.

nodes.title: WikidataIdClaim
nodes.description:
A contributor proposes the Wikidata item for an article, such as a plant or animal.

Uniqueness rule: if the propose ID already exists in ArticlesByWikidataId, we reject the event.

nodes.title: SelectWikidataId
nodes.description:
For each article, prefer an approved claim, then a pending claim. Ignore rejected claims, and sources hidden in ClaimVisibilityById (such as a censored `WRONG_ENTITY` report).

Each Wikidata ID goes to the article whose claim was accepted first. Claims from other articles for the same ID go to WikidataIdConflicts instead, and those articles get no Wikidata ID until the conflict is resolved (for example, by rejecting one of the claims, which hands the ID to the next earliest claim).

Keeps the ID provenance for presentation purposes, such as warning when Wikidata data came from an ID whose claim is not yet approved.

nodes.title: ArticlesByWikidataId
nodes.description:
Index articles by the selected Wikidata ID, with the claim as provenance. One article per ID: competing claims are in WikidataIdConflicts.

Used to match Wikidata responses to articles, and to trigger Wikidata fetching.

nodes.title: FetchWikidataEntity
nodes.description:
Request the Wikidata entity for an article's selected ID.

Fires when ArticlesByWikidataId changes for an article (a new selection or a different ID), and from a periodic sweep for refreshes. It reads only the selection: when to fetch again is the workflow's state, not the canvas's, so the canvas stays acyclic.

The fetch runs as an Effect workflow, like `FetchArticleExternalData` in `apps/server/src/wiki/external-data/workflow.ts`, which owns freshness:
- Its idempotency key combines the target, the selection and a refresh generation, so repeated triggers collapse into one execution. Manual refreshes call the workflow directly with a generation of their own, outside the canvas.
- The sweep (like `refreshExternalData` in `refresh.ts`) reads the workflow's own fetch log. A target is due when it has no fetch for its current selection, its last attempt failed over 1 hour ago, or its last success is over 2 weeks old.
- Transient errors retry inside the workflow. Permanent ones record ExternalFetchFailed and stop.
- When refreshing an unchanged selection, it first reads `lastrevid` with `wbgetentities?props=info` (50 IDs per request). If it matches the latest record, it logs the check and records no WikidataRecordReceived. A changed selection always records the full entity, so the record captures the new selection.
- A merged item (the response names another ID) is a permanent failure, `REDIRECTED`: the article's ID claim needs updating.

nodes.title: WikidataIdConflicts
nodes.description:
Wikidata IDs claimed by more than one article, keyed by Wikidata ID: the article that holds the ID in ArticlesByWikidataId, the competing claims, and when the conflict started.

Read by the moderation queue, and by article pages to warn readers that the Wikidata data may belong to another article.

nodes.title: GbifTaxonIdConflicts
nodes.description:
GBIF taxon IDs selected by more than one article, keyed by taxon ID: the article that holds the ID in ArticlesByGbifTaxonId, the competing sources (contributor claims or Wikidata records), and when the conflict started.

Read by the moderation queue, and by article pages to warn readers that the GBIF data may belong to another article.

nodes.title: BuildModerationQueue
nodes.description:
Merge everything awaiting a moderator into one list, oldest first. Each item keeps its kind and a reference to its source, so moderators open the entry in its own property for details:
- ID conflicts, from WikidataIdConflicts and GbifTaxonIdConflicts.
- Reported targets with open reports, from ClaimVisibilityById: one item per target, with every report's reason. Conduct reports go ahead of the rest, since their targets are already hidden. ReportOutcomesByPersonId ranks reports from people whose reports keep being rejected lower.
- Fetches that stopped retrying (ExternalFetchFailed), while the article still selects the failed target.
- People with repeated upheld conduct verdicts, for a blocking decision that is never automatic.
nodes.openQuestions:
- Which other sources join later: newcomers awaiting approval, revisions awaiting evaluation?
- How is an item assigned?

nodes.title: ModerationQueue
nodes.description: Items awaiting a moderator, oldest first. An item leaves the queue when its source entry disappears, such as a conflict resolved by rejecting a claim.

nodes.title: ProfileContextRecorded
nodes.description:
A person adds or deletes a context on their profile's timeline: where and how they live and produce over a period, with its own visibility and an optional label. A context is made of dimensions. Location is one of them, at any resolution (a country, a municipality, a municipality and an elevation), alongside the kind of production (agroecological, permacultural, conventional…), soil as they see it, land tenure, or living communally.

Dimensions are measured or declared. An elevation from the device's geolocation is measured; "we're at about 1,200 m" is declared.

A context never changes. When something changes, the person starts a new one, so claims stay anchored on the context they were made from. Thirty years of conventional farming followed by an agroecological settlement on the same land are two consecutive contexts with the same location. Grouping them like positions under one company can wait until we need it.

Open question: this isn't a claim about an article. Should the canvas get a third event type for profile changes?

Open question: if contexts never change, how does someone fix a typo or a wrong municipality without leaving their claims behind?

nodes.title: IndexProfileContexts
nodes.description: Keep each person's contexts in timeline order. Deleting a context removes it: claims whose provenance points to it keep their value and stay visible, but lose its dimensions.

nodes.title: ProfileContextsById
nodes.description: Contexts by ID, with their owner, period, visibility and the dimensions the person recorded.

nodes.title: PlaceClimateProfileComputed
nodes.description:
CHELSA 1981–2010 monthly normals aggregated over a gazetteer place's boundary (IBGE in Brazil, IGAC in Colombia), weighted by the area of each cell inside it. Each variable is a distribution (mean, P10, P50, P90), for the whole place and for each elevation band from the Copernicus DEM. Keeps the dataset version and the computation date. Method: the permaculture climate findings notebook (12 November 2026).

Open question: which variables come first? The notebook covered mean, minimum and maximum temperature, rainfall, PET, humidity, VPD and shortwave.

Open question: band width. 500 m bands lined up with the notebook's cuts, while 200 m bins shifted shares by up to 8 percentage points.

Open question: compute every gazetteer place in a batch, or the first time a location references one?

nodes.title: SummarizePlaceClimate
nodes.description:
Keep the latest dataset version per place, and derive what growers compare: annual mean temperature and rainfall, dry months, the rainfall pattern (one rainy season or two) and frost risk. Derive the same for each elevation band.

Open question: what counts as a dry month? Rainfall under PET, or under half of it?

Open question: compare the shape of the year rather than calendar months, so places in different hemispheres line up by their dry season?

nodes.title: ClimateProfilesByPlaceId
nodes.description: Derived climate dimensions per place and per elevation band, with the dataset they came from.

nodes.title: ResolveContextDimensions
nodes.description:
Complete each context's dimensions with what can be measured from its location: the place's ancestors, the elevation band when there's an elevation inside the place, and the climate of that band (or of the whole place without one). A location in free text adds nothing measured.

Detail grows without touching claims: claims point to contexts, so a new dimension or dataset reaches every older claim.

Open question: when the context is less visible than the claim (a public claim, a community context), what do readers see? Perhaps the dimensions without the place, or only the state.

nodes.title: ContextDimensionsById
nodes.description:
Every dimension of each context, each marked measured or declared, with its source.

Readers see claims ranked and annotated by affinity: how close the claim's context is to their own. Each dimension compares itself and explains the difference ("same rainfall pattern, 4 °C cooler"). There's never one overall score. Affinity is computed when someone reads, against their own context, so it's never stored, and it never hides a claim.

Each property declares its relevant dimensions, the ones affinity uses. Plant and animal properties default to climate and elevation.

nodes.title: ExternalFetchFailed
nodes.description:
A fetch that stopped retrying: the entity or taxon doesn't exist (`NOT_FOUND`), or the Wikidata item was merged into another (`REDIRECTED`, with the new ID). Transient errors stay inside the workflow and never show here.

It only flows downstream: the fetch triggers don't read it.

nodes.title: ClaimReported
nodes.description:
Someone reports a piece of information on an article. Anyone who can see it can report it.

The target is either a claim (`claimId`: a person's claim, an inferred claim or an ID claim) or a value projected from an external observation (the observation, the property and a value key). Value keys come from the source and the value, not from the observation, so a report keeps pointing at the same value across refreshes.

Reasons fall into two groups:
- **Conduct**: `ABUSIVE` (racism, classism, queerphobia, misogyny…), `SPAM`, `FALSE` (deliberately false: fake news, vandalism) and `DANGEROUS` (could hurt someone who follows it, such as eating a toxic part).
- **Quality**: `MISTAKEN`, `OFF_TOPIC` and `WRONG_ENTITY` (the article's Wikidata or GBIF ID points at another taxon; report the ID claim or the selected ID).

Disagreeing isn't a report: on situated properties, make your own claim, and on canonical ones, propose a correction. A person has at most one open report per target.

exampleData.note: In Brazil, "mimosa" usually means Mimosa pudica.

nodes.title: ClaimReportSettled
nodes.description:
A moderator's verdict on all of a target's open reports at once: `CENSOR`, `KEEP` or `KEEP_WITH_WARNING` (with a note readers see). It records the reports it settles, who decided and why, and the target's authors as captured when settling.

A `CENSOR` verdict on a `WRONG_ENTITY` report works like rejecting the ID: the selection moves to the next source. Reports on values that were already approved contest an earlier evaluation, so a moderator other than the one who approved should settle them.

exampleData.note: Also used for Mimosa pudica in Brazil.

nodes.title: ResolveClaimVisibility
nodes.description:
Derive each reported target's visibility from its reports and verdicts:
- An open conduct report hides the target from everyone but its authors and moderators until a verdict. `KEEP` shows it again.
- Open quality reports change nothing readers see until a verdict.
- `CENSOR` hides it. For external values, the same value from the same source stays hidden on later refreshes; a different value from that source shows normally.
- `KEEP_WITH_WARNING` shows it with the moderator's note.

After a verdict, new reports with a reason it already settled join that verdict instead of reopening the target. A new reason reopens it.

Also tallies outcomes per person: upheld conduct verdicts against the target's authors, and how each reporter's reports were settled. Upheld quality verdicts count against no one, and an inferred claim's verdict counts against the inference, not the publication's author.

nodes.title: ClaimVisibilityById
nodes.description:
Visibility of every reported target, keyed by claim ID or value key: `HIDDEN` (with the reason, and whether an open report or a verdict hides it), `WARNED` (with the moderator's note), or `UNDER_REVIEW` (open quality reports only, still shown). Targets without an entry are visible.

Read by every transformation that resolves values for readers, so hidden values also stay out of summaries, counts and selections. Read by the moderation queue for open reports, grouped per target.
nodes.openQuestions:
Can we have a better data structure?

- I bet `visibility: "HIDDEN_WHILE_REVIEWING"` is much better than having an extra "hiddenBy"
- top level `reasons` feels out of place when we have openReports.
- why not just `reports` with the status of open | closed or something like that?

wikidata:Q757123:names:pt:mimosa.note: Also used for Mimosa pudica in Brazil.

nodes.title: ReportOutcomesByPersonId
nodes.description:
Per person: upheld conduct verdicts on their claims, and how their own reports were settled.

The moderation queue uses it to move a person's other recent claims up after an upheld conduct verdict, to list people with repeated conduct verdicts for a blocking decision, and to rank reports from people whose reports keep being rejected lower. Their reports still count.
